rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all 10 compounds and locate their elution window while limiting late-elution risk. The retention and resolution pattern will guide narrower-window, slope, and temperature tests.

Change only gradient duration to measure how the crowded early cluster responds to a shallower slope. This diagnostic run will distinguish slope-sensitive pairs from those that need temperature-driven selectivity changes.

Test temperature selectivity at the original gradient slope, since lengthening improved the early cluster but incurred a time penalty. Higher temperature may separate the critical peaks while keeping the last peak within 10 minutes.

At 60 C only one pair remains below target, with nearly two minutes of retention-time headroom. Test a shallower gradient to improve that pair and determine whether full resolution is reachable near the 10-minute limit.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a steeper slope instead. This should improve that pair and shorten elution, while checking whether the neighboring pair retains sufficient resolution.

Probe the opposite temperature extreme to map selectivity in the crowded cluster; slope changes alone have not fully resolved it at 60 C. This diagnostic may incur a time penalty, but could reveal a different elution order with better separation.

Shift the starting organic fraction upward while keeping the slope close to injection 3 to test window-driven selectivity in the critical cluster. The first peak may become less retained, so its retention and separation will be checked carefully.

Injection 7 reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method, checking the two early pairs with the smallest resolution margins.

Reduce the final organic fraction to make the 8-minute gradient slightly shallower and recover the two marginal early separations. The last peak previously eluted near 0.64 organic, so 0.85 should remain sufficient while potentially beating injection 7's elution time.

Raise the gradient window by 0.05 while preserving injection 9's slope to seek earlier elution without sacrificing critical-pair resolution. Monitor the first peaks for excessive compression as starting organic increases.

Change only temperature from injection 9 to measure local selectivity around the fully resolved method. This tests whether a modest temperature reduction creates resolution headroom that could support a faster gradient.

Test a slightly steeper slope than injection 9 using a shorter gradient ending above the estimated last-peak elution fraction. This targets a faster fully resolved method, with the early critical pair expected to be close to R = 1.5.

Injection 12 still has a subthreshold pair despite its rounded CRF of 1.000, so injection 9 remains the faster confirmed fully resolved method. Test a shallower gradient at the higher starting fraction to recover the separation lost in injection 10 while retaining its favorable selectivity for the neighboring pair.

The higher starting fraction requires slower elution without improving the best score, so return to 0.15 and modestly flatten the gradient. This tests for a larger minimum-resolution margin while keeping all peaks comfortably within 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one grid step from injection 12 to recover its marginal critical pair while retaining a six-minute programmed gradient. The last peak should elute near the gradient endpoint; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved benchmark.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test whether a shallower, trimmed gradient increases the minimum-resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. The endpoint is near the expected last-peak elution fraction, so only a short final hold should be needed.

Reduce the endpoint one step from injection 13 to bring its lone marginal pair above R = 1.5. This tests whether the higher starting fraction can provide full resolution with earlier last-peak elution than injection 16.

Test the untried intermediate starting fraction at the same slope as injection 12 to check for a better balance between the two critical early separations. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method and the benchmark for this shorter-gradient alternative.

Refine between injections 9 and 14 with a single endpoint step, seeking a little more critical-pair margin than injection 9 at a smaller time cost than injection 14. The maximum CRF is already secured, and this method should retain full resolution comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test the remaining endpoint step between fully resolved injection 9 and slightly under-resolved injection 8. This directly checks whether the last-peak time can be reduced below 6.04 minutes while preserving every pair at R >= 1.5.

Test a slope between injections 13 and 17 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary at the higher starting fraction. The lower endpoint may move the last peak into the hold, so assess its retention alongside the marginal early pair.

Preserve injection 14's fully resolving slope but end the gradient two minutes earlier to reduce final organic consumption. Check whether the last peak elutes promptly during the hold without compromising the maximum CRF; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Refine the fully resolved region between injections 14 and 16, seeking additional critical-pair margin with less retention-time cost than injection 16. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed method attaining the maximum CRF.

Test the remaining endpoint step between injections 16 and 23 to refine the tradeoff between resolution margin and elution time within the maximum-CRF region. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use the final injection to test a narrower six-minute gradient expected to retain full resolution, with the last compound finishing during the hold below 10 minutes. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, and the campaign has already reached the maximum CRF.
